subtopics.title: From Owner to Shareholder — the Company Form

questions.question: A company becomes a separate legal person when:
options: Its Memorandum of Incorporation is registered with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission
Its first shares trade on the JSE
Its first dividend is declared
Its auditor signs the first audit report

questions.question: Continuity of existence means that:
options: Directors may never resign
Shareholders can die, emigrate or sell out and the company carries on unchanged
The company may never be liquidated
Issued shares may never change hands

questions.question: A private company (Pty Ltd) differs from a public company (Ltd) in that a private company:
options: Is not a separate legal person
Pays no income tax
May not offer its shares to the public and restricts their transfer
Has shareholders with unlimited liability

questions.question: The law requires a public company to appoint an independent auditor because:
options: The JSE sets the share price
SARS cannot assess companies without one
Shareholders are not allowed to attend the AGM
Directors manage money belonging to other people, so an outside check reports to the owners on their stewardship

subtopics.title: Issuing Shares and Buying Them Back

questions.question: Naledi Ltd issues 200 000 no par value shares at R8,00 each. The correct entry is:
options: Debit Bank R1 600 000; credit Ordinary Share Capital R1 600 000 — the full issue price goes to share capital
Debit Bank R1 600 000; credit Share Capital R1 000 000 and Share Premium R600 000
Debit Ordinary Share Capital R1 600 000; credit Bank R1 600 000
Debit Bank R1 600 000; credit Retained Income R1 600 000

questions.question: After the issue, share capital is R4 600 000 for 800 000 shares in issue. The average issue price is:
Naledi Ltd buys back 40 000 shares at R9,00 each when the average issue price is R5,75. Ordinary Share Capital is debited with:
options: R360 000 — the full amount paid
R130 000 — the excess over the average
R230 000 — 40 000 shares at the average issue price of R5,75
Nothing; the whole payment comes from retained income

questions.question: After the buy-back of 40 000 shares, the shares repurchased are:
options: Kept in the safe for resale next year
Given to the directors as fees
Entitled to the final dividend
Cancelled — 760 000 shares remain in issue and the cancelled shares earn no further dividends

subtopics.title: Income Tax and Dividends in the Ledger

questions.question: Each provisional tax payment during the year is recorded as:
options: Debit SARS — Income Tax; credit Bank
Debit Bank; credit SARS — Income Tax
Debit Income Tax; credit Retained Income
Debit Shareholders for Dividends; credit Bank

questions.question: Provisional payments totalled R360 000 and the final charge is 27 percent of R1 500 000. The SARS — Income Tax account closes with:
options: A debit balance of R45 000 — a refund due
A credit balance of R45 000 — a current liability still owed to SARS
A credit balance of R405 000
A nil balance

questions.question: The final dividend of 50 cents per share was declared on 28 February, after the buy-back left 760 000 shares in issue. The final dividend is:
options: R380 000 — 760 000 shares times 50 cents, on the shares in issue at the declaration date

questions.question: The interim dividend of R240 000 does NOT appear under current liabilities at year-end because:
options: Interim dividends are not appropriations of profit
It was smaller than the final dividend
It was refunded by the shareholders
It was declared and paid within the year — the cash already left, so nothing is owing

subtopics.title: Loans, Directors' Fees and Audit Fees

questions.question: A loan of R800 000 at 10 percent with capitalised interest, with instalments of R180 000 paid during the year, closes at:
options: R700 000 — the loan grows by R80 000 interest before the R180 000 of payments reduces it

questions.question: Although the capitalised interest of R80 000 never left the bank account separately, it is:
options: Ignored until the loan is repaid in full
Still a full expense on the income statement, credited to the Loan account
Deducted from share capital
Treated as a dividend to Kopano Bank

questions.question: Directors' fees are classified as:
options: An appropriation of profit after tax
A current liability
An operating expense — payment for the work of managing, deducted in arriving at net profit
Part of ordinary share capital

questions.question: An auditor whose fee depends on giving a clean opinion, or who accepts lavish hospitality from the directors, has:
options: Simply negotiated good terms
Improved the reliability of the report
No effect on the audit, since only SARS relies on it
Surrendered the independence that gives the audit report its value to shareholders

subtopics.title: The Spaza That Became a Company

questions.question: Naledi registers a company and sells slices of the business because:
options: The expansion needs more money than her savings and bank loans can supply
The law forces every spaza to incorporate
Companies pay no tax on profits
Shareholders will work in the new branches for free

questions.question: If the company fails, a person who bought slices loses:
options: Their house and car, up to the company's debts
Only what they paid for the slices — limited liability stops the loss there
Nothing, because the directors repay them
Their salary from the company

questions.question: In the loaf picture, the authorised share capital is:
options: The slices already handed over the counter
The price of one slice
The most slices the loaf may ever be cut into — the ceiling written in the MOI
The profit on each slice sold

questions.question: The tension at the heart of the company form is that:
options: Companies may not borrow from banks
Every shareholder must also be a director
Auditors manage the business day to day
The directors spending the money are not the shareholders who own it — which is why the AGM and the audit exist

questions.question: The fresh slices sell at R8,00 while the old slices averaged R5,00 because:
options: A piece of a bigger, stronger business costs more than a piece of the old spaza did
The law requires each new issue to be priced above the last
SARS sets the issue price
The old shareholders are refunded the R3,00 difference

questions.question: The R360 000 paid in the buy-back is drawn from the books as:
options: All R360 000 from retained income
R230 000 from share capital at the R5,75 average, and R130 000 from retained income
All R360 000 from share capital
R180 000 from each account

questions.question: The retiring shareholder's payout is described as one cheque with two sources because:
options: The bank and SARS each paid half
Half is a loan he must repay later
It refunds what the slices contributed to capital, topped up with a farewell share of saved-up profits
Dividends and fees are always paid together

questions.question: After the 40 000 slices are cancelled, each remaining slice is:
options: Worth exactly what it was before, by law
Entitled to a cash refund
Converted into a loan to the company
A slightly larger fraction of the business, because the same yard is now divided into 760 000 slices

questions.question: The company's tax guesses added up to R360 000 and the counted tax came to R405 000, so at year-end:
options: R45 000 is still owed to SARS — a debt on the balance sheet
SARS owes the company R45 000
The full R405 000 is still owing
Nothing is owing, because provisional tax always settles the year

questions.question: A dividend only becomes something the company owes when:
options: A shareholder demands payment in writing
The directors declare it — until then no shareholder is owed anything
The auditor approves it
The shares were originally bought from the company itself

questions.question: The October dividend used 800 000 slices and the February dividend used 760 000 slices because:
options: The dividend rate fell during the year
New slices were sold in January
The buy-back trimmed the company to 760 000 slices before the final dividend was declared
Final dividends by law use fewer shares

questions.question: A director who also owns slices of the company is paid:
options: Only dividends, since directors may not earn fees
Only fees, since directors may not own shares
One combined amount called a bonus
Through two doors — directors' fees for the managing and dividends for the owning — recorded in different places
